openSource.title: Open source
openSource.description: Draggy is free software under the Apache 2.0 license. What the license allows, where the source is, and how each model's license applies.
openSource.ogDescription: Draggy is free software under the Apache 2.0 license. What the license allows, where the source is, and how each model's license applies.
openSource.lede: You can use, change and share Draggy's code under the Apache License 2.0. The models it runs have their own licenses.
openSource.allowsLead: Draggy's source is published under the Apache License, Version 2.0. You can:
openSource.allow1: Use Draggy for any purpose, including paid work.
openSource.allow2: Change it and build your own version.
openSource.allow3: Share copies of it, or of your changes.
openSource.allow4: Sell copies, or a product built on it.
openSource.keepLead: If you share Draggy or a changed version, you must:
openSource.keep1: Give everyone who receives it a copy of the license.
openSource.keep2: Keep the copyright, patent, trademark and attribution notices in the source.
openSource.keep3: Mark the files you changed as changed.
openSource.keep4: Include the text of the NOTICE file, if the copy has one.
openSource.keepTail: The license does not let you use the Draggy name or logo, apart from describing where the code comes from.
openSource.earlier: Earlier versions released under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later keep that license for those versions.
openSource.source: The source is on GitHub at github.com/Lucki74/draggy. The full license is in the repository, with the NOTICE file, the contribution guide and the security policy.
openSource.models: A model is a separate work, and its maker sets its license. The license is shown on the model's Hugging Face page. Read it there before you use or share a model.
openSource.leaves: For what leaves your computer, read the privacy page of the documentation.

pricing.free2: The source code, under the Apache License 2.0.

faq.heading: Questions
faq.a1: Yes. It costs nothing and has no paid tier. A provider you add bills you on its own terms.
faq.a2: Some things do: downloading models and speech models, web search, update checks, the ad blocker's filter lists, and any provider or cloud voice you add. By default, chat, code, document search and voice run on your computer.
faq.q3: Do I need a graphics card?
faq.a3: No. Draggy picks a model your hardware can run. A dedicated graphics card usually makes it faster. Choosing a model lists the models for each graphics card size.
faq.q4: Can I use ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini with it?
faq.a4: Yes. Sign in with a ChatGPT or Claude plan, or add an API key for Google Gemini or another provider, from Settings, Providers. The built-in engine stays the default.
faq.a5: Draggy sends requests when you start them, such as model downloads and web searches. It also sends some on its own, such as update checks and ad blocker lists. Your conversations leave your computer only if you add a cloud provider. The privacy policy names the services involved.
faq.q6: Can I use models I already have?
faq.a6: Yes, with local servers. Start one, then press Scan under Settings, Providers. Draggy finds servers such as Ollama and LM Studio that run on this computer.
faq.q7: Does it ask before it changes things?
faq.a7: Commands ask first unless you choose Turbo or YOLO. In the default Accept edits mode, ordinary file edits go ahead without asking, but moving and deleting files ask first. Ask first also asks before each edit. Plan only changes nothing. Every edit can be undone.
faq.q8: Why does my computer warn me when I open it?
faq.a8: Draggy's build is not signed with a developer certificate yet. Windows shows a warning on the first run. The steps to get past it are on the download page.
faq.a9: Windows and Linux check for a new version at launch and every six hours. On Windows, an update found at launch installs in the startup window, and you can start without updating.
faq.a10: The app's screens are in English, French, Spanish and Russian. The natural voice speaks English, French and Spanish.

home.v1Title: Your files stay on your disk, by default.
home.v1Text: Draggy works in the folder you choose and keeps chats on your disk. A provider you add receives the files its model reads.
home.v2Text: There is no paid tier. A provider you add bills you on its own terms.
home.v3Text: Read the code, build it yourself and change it.
home.f1Text: Ask a question, and Draggy reads the pages and answers with the sources it used.
home.f2Text: It edits files in your folder and shows each change as a diff you can undo.
home.f3Text: Commands ask first unless you choose Turbo or YOLO. In the default Accept edits mode, ordinary edits go ahead, but moving and deleting files ask first.
home.f4Text: Speak your question and hear the answer.
home.f5Text: Pages open in a browser of its own, with its own session and tracker blocking.
home.logosLabel: Providers and engines you can connect
home.s2: Connect the providers you already use.
home.s3: Nothing changes until you say yes.
